headline: Law extends federal approval for U.S. Geological Survey research on Great Lakes fisheries through 2030.
what_it_does: This law renews approval for the U.S. Geological Survey to carry out research and monitoring of fish in the Great Lakes through fiscal year 2030. The work is done through the Great Lakes Science Center and supports fisheries shared by the U.S. and Canada. It can include studying invasive species, studying fish populations, and using biological tools to help guide fishery management decisions.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. Geological Survey and its Great Lakes Science Center
who_it_affects.how: The agency keeps its authority to conduct Great Lakes fishery research and monitoring through fiscal year 2030.

who_it_affects.group: Agencies that manage Great Lakes fisheries in the U.S. and Canada
who_it_affects.how: They can continue to rely on this federal research when making fishery management decisions.

who_it_affects.group: People who fish or work in fishing in the Great Lakes region
who_it_affects.how: The fish populations they depend on will keep being studied and monitored, including for invasive species.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 26, 2025; authorization runs through fiscal year 2030.
